code: set.seed(92327001) ratings <- expand.grid(   Criterion = paste0("C", 1:5), Task = paste0("T", 1:3),   Person = sprintf("P%03d", 1:80), stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) ability <- rnorm(80) local_effect <- matrix(rnorm(80 * 3, sd = sqrt(.8)), 80, 3) p <- match(ratings$Person, sprintf("P%03d", 1:80)) t <- match(ratings$Task, paste0("T", 1:3)) eta <- ability[p] + local_effect[cbind(p, t)] w <- exp(cbind(0, eta + .6, 2 * eta)) probability <- w / rowSums(w) u <- runif(nrow(ratings)) ratings$Score <- as.integer(u > probability[, 1]) +   as.integer(u > rowSums(probability[, 1:2])) testlet_fit <- fit_mfrm_testlet(   ratings, "Person", "Score", "Task", score_levels = 0:2,   quad_points = 61 ) independent_fit <- fit_mfrm_testlet(   ratings, "Person", "Score", "Task", score_levels = 0:2,   testlet_variance = 0, quad_points = 121 ) for (fit in list(testlet_fit, independent_fit)) {   stopifnot(fit$checks$NumericalReady, fit$checks$InformationPositive) } data.frame(   Model = c("Testlet", "Independent"),   AbilityVariance = c(testlet_fit$calibration$person_variance,                      independent_fit$calibration$person_variance),   LocalVariance = c(testlet_fit$calibration$variance, 0) ) #>         Model AbilityVariance LocalVariance #> 1     Testlet        1.334107     0.6950509 #> 2 Independent        1.078343     0.0000000

code: normal_rule <- function(n) {   jacobi <- matrix(0, n, n)   jacobi[cbind(1:(n - 1), 2:n)] <- sqrt(1:(n - 1))   e <- eigen(jacobi + t(jacobi), symmetric = TRUE)   list(nodes = e$values, weights = e$vectors[1, ]^2) }  pattern_mass <- function(fit, membership, patterns, order) {   rule <- normal_rule(order)   theta <- fit$calibration$person_sd * rule$nodes   gamma <- sqrt(fit$calibration$variance) * rule$nodes   answer <- numeric(nrow(patterns))   for (h in seq_along(theta)) {     logw <- outer(theta[h] + gamma, 0:2) -       matrix(c(0, cumsum(fit$calibration$steps)), order, 3, byrow = TRUE)     prob <- exp(logw - apply(logw, 1, max))     prob <- prob / rowSums(prob)     conditional <- rep(1, nrow(patterns))     for (block in split(seq_along(membership), membership)) {       block_prob <- matrix(1, order, nrow(patterns))       for (j in block) {         block_prob <- block_prob * prob[, patterns[, j] + 1L, drop = FALSE]       }       conditional <- conditional * as.vector(crossprod(rule$weights, block_prob))     }     answer <- answer + rule$weights[h] * conditional   }   answer }  evaluate_parallel_plan <- function(fit, membership) {   stopifnot(inherits(fit, "mfrm_testlet"),     length(fit$input$columns$facets) == 0L,     identical(as.numeric(fit$input$score_levels), 0:2 + 0),     length(membership) == 4L, !anyNA(membership))   patterns <- as.matrix(expand.grid(rep(list(0:2), 4)))   data <- data.frame(Person = rep(sprintf("Y%02d", 1:81), each = 4),     Task = rep(membership, 81), Score = as.vector(t(patterns)))   scores <- predict(fit, data, quad_points = 61)   stopifnot(identical(scores$table$Person, sprintf("Y%02d", 1:81)),             all(scores$table$Status == "available_conditional"))   low <- pattern_mass(fit, membership, patterns, 61)   probability <- pattern_mass(fit, membership, patterns, 121)   tab <- scores$table   v <- fit$calibration$person_variance   expected_variance <- sum(probability * tab$ConditionalSD^2)   stopifnot(abs(sum(probability) - 1) < 1e-8,     max(abs(low - probability)) < 1e-8,     abs(sum(probability * tab$Estimate)) < 1e-7,     abs(sum(probability * (tab$ConditionalSD^2 + tab$Estimate^2)) - v) < 1e-7)   list(scores = scores, probability = probability, patterns = patterns,     membership = membership, summary = data.frame(       RMSPosteriorSD = sqrt(expected_variance),       ModelImpliedEAPReliability = 1 - expected_variance / v)) }

title: mfrmr Visual Diagnostics
text: Use plot_type = "measure" relate measures fair scores, "scatter" compare observed fair scores, "difference" rank gaps. FairM uses mean reference measures; FairZ uses zero reference measures. FairZ expected score internal score scale, z-score. Observed-minus-fair gaps also reflect assignment person mix, establish rater bias. Use draw = TRUE draw base-R version. Titles notes remain returned object hidden figure. annotation controls apply Wright, expected-score pathway, CCC plots; change readiness interval eligibility. Keep applicable notes surrounding caption report. plotting helpers documented options. Fair-score intervals remain diagnostic-(CI_Eligible = FALSE), full-refit coverage unverified. RSM/PCM plots propagate focal measure SE, holding thresholds reference measures fixed; require fitted model, just stored fair-average bundle. GPCM-MML plots use available structural delta-method SEs non-Person rows, conditioning Person EAP/reference means. table option fair_se = TRUE supplies GPCM route, RSM/PCM fair-score SEs. Historical table SE columns describe measures. Difference-view whiskers hold observed means fixed confidence intervals observed-minus-fair gap. Expected-score CCC curves use six line types: solid, dashed, dotted, dotdash, longdash, twodash. Fair-score plots use six point shapes. encodings repeat larger sets; select facets use panels keep grayscale figure readable. Check labels line separation intended output size rather relying color gray levels alone.

Re-estimates model new_data anchors fixed via fit_mfrm(..., anchors = anchor_table). Runs diagnose_mfrm() anchored fit. Computes element-level differences (new estimate minus baseline estimate) every common element. helper refuses baseline unless current readiness record InferenceReady = TRUE. Also confirm compatible model, score coding, orientation, population conventions, document anchor labels denote elements invariant meaning. function checks object shape receiving-data anchor compatibility, establish substantive conditions. Fixing parameters can identify coordinates; create observed common-rating links. model method arguments default baseline fit's settings calibration framework remains consistent.  Elements present anchor table absent new data handled according anchor_policy: "warn" (default) emits message, "error" stops execution, "silent" ignores silently. returned drift table best interpreted anchored consistency check. facet fixed anchor_facets, anchored levels constrained new run, reported differences independent drift analysis. genuine cross-wave drift monitoring, fit waves separately use detect_anchor_drift() resulting fits. Element-level differences calculated every element appears baseline new calibration: $$\Delta_e = \hat{\delta}_{e,\text{new}} - \hat{\delta}_{e,\text{base}}$$ element flagged \(|\Delta_e| > 0.5\) logits \(|\Delta_e / SE_{\Delta_e}| > 2.0\), \(SE_{\Delta_e} = \sqrt{SE_{\mathrm{base}}^2 + SE_{\mathrm{new}}^2}\). SE_Diff plug-independence calculation. propagate baseline-anchor uncertainty cross-fit covariance, anchored estimates new fit constrained rather independently re-estimated. title: Fit new data anchored to a baseline calibration — anchor_to_baseline
code: # \donttest{ # Deliberately linked teaching waves: both retain the same rater and # criterion identities from one synthetic calibration design. toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core") people <- unique(toy$Person) # Two balanced 12-Person waves retain every Rater and Criterion. d1 <- toy[toy$Person %in% people[1:12], , drop = FALSE] d2 <- toy[toy$Person %in% people[13:24], , drop = FALSE] fit1 <- fit_mfrm(d1, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",                  method = "MML", quad_points = 7, maxit = 30) res <- anchor_to_baseline(d2, fit1, "Person",                           c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",                           anchor_facets = "Criterion") summary(res) #> --- Anchored Fit Summary --- #> Inference-ready: TRUE  #> Optimizer returned code 0: TRUE | Status: converged  #> Anchors used: 4 | Common elements: 4 | Flagged: 0  #>  #> Drift by facet: #>      Facet N Mean_Drift Max_Drift N_Flagged #>  Criterion 4          0         0         0 head(res$drift[, c("Facet", "Level", "Drift", "Flag")]) #> # A tibble: 4 × 4 #>   Facet     Level        Drift Flag  #>   <chr>     <chr>        <dbl> <lgl> #> 1 Criterion Accuracy         0 FALSE #> 2 Criterion Content          0 FALSE #> 3 Criterion Language         0 FALSE #> 4 Criterion Organization     0 FALSE res$baseline_anchors[1:3, ] #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   Facet     Level     Anchor #>   <chr>     <chr>      <dbl> #> 1 Criterion Accuracy  0.210  #> 2 Criterion Content  -0.443  #> 3 Criterion Language  0.0979 # }

text: Post-hoc normal-model shrinkage helper augments mfrm_fit descriptive empirical-Bayes adjustments non-person facet. shrinkage variance \(\hat{\tau}^2\) estimated method moments facet-level point estimates standard errors: $$\hat{\tau}^2 = \max\!\left(0,   \frac{1}{K}\sum_{j=1}^{K}\hat{\delta}_j^{2} -   \overline{\mathrm{SE}^2}\right),$$ zero chosen shrinkage target moment calculated complete finite estimate/positive-SE pairs. sum--zero identification constraint establish known population mean independent errors. shrinkage factor \(B_j = \mathrm{SE}_j^2 / (\hat{\tau}^2 + \mathrm{SE}_j^2)\), \(\hat{\delta}_j^{EB} = (1-B_j)\hat{\delta}_j\) \(\mathrm{ShrunkSE}_j = \sqrt{(1-B_j)\mathrm{SE}_j^2}\).

code: # \donttest{ toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core") fit <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",                 method = "JML", maxit = 300) fit_eb <- apply_empirical_bayes_shrinkage(fit) fit_eb$shrinkage_report #>       Facet NLevels NLevelsUsed       Tau2     MeanSE2 MeanShrinkage #> 1     Rater       4           4 0.06402776 0.009499649     0.1291985 #> 2 Criterion       4           4 0.05258949 0.009500118     0.1530052 #>   EffectiveDF          Method PriorSource Note SupportsFormalInference #> 1    3.483206 empirical_bayes   empirical <NA>                   FALSE #> 2    3.387979 empirical_bayes   empirical <NA>                   FALSE #>                                                                                                                                                             Interpretation #> 1 Descriptive zero-centered adjustment; plug-in SEs/bands omit prior-variance uncertainty and cross-level covariance. Zero SE after full pooling is not perfect precision. #> 2 Descriptive zero-centered adjustment; plug-in SEs/bands omit prior-variance uncertainty and cross-level covariance. Zero SE after full pooling is not perfect precision. # Look for: # - `Tau2` is the estimated between-level prior variance per facet. #   `Tau2 = 0` fully pools eligible estimates at zero #   (`MeanShrinkage = 1`). Zero plug-in SE is not perfect precision. # - `MeanShrinkage` near 0 = little movement, near 1 = heavy pooling #   toward the chosen zero target; inspect the SEs and prior variance. # - `EffectiveDF` sums retained weights over eligible levels, conditional #   on the chosen prior variance; it is not degrees of freedom for testing. head(fit_eb$facets$others[, c("Facet", "Level", "Estimate",                                "ShrunkEstimate", "ShrinkageFactor")]) #>       Facet    Level   Estimate ShrunkEstimate ShrinkageFactor #> 1     Rater      R01 -0.1957463     -0.1705317       0.1288124 #> 2     Rater      R02 -0.3287812     -0.2861288       0.1297287 #> 3     Rater      R03  0.1910898      0.1665008       0.1286778 #> 4     Rater      R04  0.3334376      0.2902324       0.1295752 #> 5 Criterion Accuracy  0.2487265      0.2106950       0.1529051 #> 6 Criterion  Content -0.4150443     -0.3508124       0.1547591 # Look for: rows where `ShrinkageFactor` is large (close to 1) had #   their estimates pulled most strongly toward the facet mean (0). # }

Instead, synthesizes four package-native evidence sources: compare_mfrm() -data model comparison non-person facet measures fit bounded GPCM slope table compute_information() design-weighted information redistribution result intended substantive review, automatic model selection. particular, better-fitting GPCM interpreted reason discard equal-weighting Rasch-family route. fitted GPCM contains one slope every level one designated facet, one common slope simultaneous criterion--rater slope blocks. overview records slope owner, step owner, level count, free relative slope contrasts, whether supplied reference exact unit-slope PCM response-kernel reduction. formal PCM-versus-GPCM chi-square LRT unavailable. Free-slope GPCM also lacks inference checks required information-criterion ranking, even MML. returned comparison_contract records applicable comparison restrictions; observed changes fit, scores information remain descriptive. JML log-likelihood increase promoted automatic PCM-versus-GPCM model selection unpenalized GPCM contains additional slope parameters. FACETS may serve direct comparator PCM/JML side ; post-fit discrimination statistic jointly estimated free-slope GPCM counterpart.

title: Build a category curve export bundle (preferred alias) — category_curves_report
text: Preferred high-level API category-probability curve exports. Returns tidy curve coordinates summary metadata quick plotting/report integration without calling low-level helpers directly. expected-score table also carries per-curve score variance information function. GPCM, information column follows Muraki/Samejima identity \(^2 \mathrm{Var}(X \mid \theta)\); RSM / PCM, reduces usual score variance discrimination fixed one. category_information table decomposes total category-level contributions, \(^2 P_k(\theta)(k - E[X \mid \theta])^2\), whose sum equals reported information theta value. cumulative_probabilities table follows FACETS / Winsteps graph convention accumulating modeled probabilities across ordered categories (P(X <= k) default, P(X >= k) also returned flipped curves). cumulative_boundaries reports approximate theta values P(X <= k) = .5, BoundaryStatus CrossingCount avoid -interpreting boundaries outside requested theta range multiple crossings. reference-profile curves. Estimated step parameters , GPCM, step-facet group's estimated slope retained, additive facet main effects fitted interactions fixed zero. CurveBasis PredictorOffset columns, corresponding entries settings, make conditioning explicit. Thus curves represent arbitrary observed Person--facet cell.

title: Estimate bias and interaction screening terms — estimate_bias

title: Build facet variability diagnostics with fixed/random reference tests — facets_chisq_table
text: table data.frame contains: Facet Facet name. Levels Number estimated levels facet. MeanMeasure, SD Mean standard deviation level measures. FixedChiSq, FixedDF, FixedProb Fixed-effect chi-square test (null hypothesis: levels equal). Significant result means facet elements differ measurement error alone. RandomChiSq, RandomDF, RandomProb, RandomVar Random-effect test (null hypothesis: variation equals random sample single population). Significant result suggests systematic heterogeneity beyond sampling variation. FixedFlag, RandomFlag Logical flags significance.

text: guide separates mean-square size ZSTD standardization. Infit outfit MnSq values answer large residual noise predictability signal . ZSTD values standardize MnSq values using degrees-- freedom convention Wilson-Hilferty-style transformation, ZSTD can differ even underlying MnSq values nearly identical. Two boundaries sit upstream df comparison. First, residual basis: method = "MML" fits evaluate residuals shrunken EAP person measures, whereas FACETS evaluates JMLE estimates, MnSq values can differ standardization applied; refit method = "JML" comparison requires JMLE-style residual basis. Second, small df: mfrmr returns NA ZSTD df < 1 Wilson-Hilferty transformation numerically unstable , FACETS/Winsteps WHEXACT can continue linear approximation, sparse cells can show NA finite external value without indicating fit difference.

title: mfrmr: Many-Facet Ordered-Response Modeling in R — mfrmr-package
text: Marginal Maximum Likelihood (MML) MML integrates person ability distribution using Gauss-Hermite quadrature, broader marginal-likelihood framework introduced Bock & Aitkin (1981) IRT: $$L = \prod_{n} \int P(\mathbf{X}_n \mid \theta, \boldsymbol{\delta})   \, \phi(\theta) \, d\theta   \approx \prod_{n} \sum_{q=1}^{Q} w_q \,   P(\mathbf{X}_n \mid \theta_q, \boldsymbol{\delta})$$ \(\phi(\theta)\) assumed normal prior \((\theta_q, w_q)\) quadrature nodes weights.  Person estimates obtained post-hoc via Expected Posteriori (EAP): $$\hat{\theta}_n^{\mathrm{EAP}} =   \frac{\sum_q \theta_q \, w_q \, L(\mathbf{X}_n \mid \theta_q)}        {\sum_q w_q \, L(\mathbf{X}_n \mid \theta_q)}$$ MML estimate one fixed person parameter per respondent therefore avoids JML incidental-parameter mechanism. structural inference nevertheless conditional specified population distribution, response model, quadrature approximation, regularity conditions; automatic small-sample guarantee. Note: Bock & Aitkin (1981) canonical citation Gauss-Hermite-quadrature MML framework. default mfrmr engine (mml_engine = "direct") optimises marginal log-likelihood direct gradient methods (BFGS / L-BFGS-B), Bock & Aitkin's signature EM algorithm. "em" "hybrid" engines follow EM template use selected gradient-based M-step rather B&'s probit IRLS, target polytomous Rasch family rather B&'s 2PL probit model. Joint Maximum Likelihood (JML) JML estimates person facet parameters simultaneously fixed effects maximising joint log-likelihood \(\ell(\boldsymbol{\theta}, \boldsymbol{\delta} \mid \mathbf{X})\) directly.  assume parametric person distribution, can advantageous population shape strongly non-normal. incidental-parameter concern simply small-person-sample issue: structural-parameter bias can persist number persons increases number ratings items per person remains fixed (Neyman & Scott, 1948). package still accepts "JMLE" backward-compatible alias, user-facing summaries documentation use "JML" public label. title: Plot inter-rater agreement diagnostics using base R — plot_interrater_agreement
text: Inter-rater agreement plots summarize pairwise consistency chosen rater facet.  Agreement statistics computed observations share person context-facet levels, ensuring comparisons reflect identical rating targets. Exact agreement proportion matched observations raters assigned category score.  expected agreement line shows proportion expected fitted model, averaging products category probabilities matched rating contexts. model-based baseline, chance-corrected agreement coefficient. Pairwise correlation Pearson correlation scores assigned rater pair matched observations. difference plot describes directional score differences (mean signed difference x-axis: positive = Rater 1 assigned higher scores) total inconsistency (mean absolute difference y-axis). title: Plot inter-rater agreement diagnostics using base R — plot_interrater_agreement
text: "exact" (default) Bar chart exact agreement proportion rater pair.  Expected agreement overlaid connected circles. Horizontal reference line exact_warn.  Bars colored red observed agreement falls warning threshold. "corr" Bar chart pairwise Pearson correlation rater pair.  Reference line corr_warn.  Ordered correlation (lowest first).  Low correlations suggest inconsistent rank ordering persons raters. "difference" Scatter plot.  X-axis: mean signed score difference (Rater 1 \(-\) Rater 2); positive values indicate Rater 1 assigned higher scores. observed-score contrast distinct fitted rater-severity parameter. Y-axis: mean absolute difference (overall disagreement magnitude).  Points colored red flagged.  Vertical reference 0.

title: Plot a base-R QC dashboard — plot_qc_dashboard
text: Recommended panel order fast review: Category counts + Infit/Outfit (row 1): first-pass model screening. Category bars roughly track expected line; Infit/Outfit points often reviewed heuristic 0.5–1.5 band. Unexpected responses + Displacement (row 2): element-level outliers.  Sparse points small displacements desirable. Inter-rater + Chi-square (row 3): facet-level comparability. Read screening panels: higher agreement suggests stronger scoring consistency, significant fixed chi-square indicates detectable facet spread current model. Separation/Reliability (row 3): approximate screening precision. Higher separation indicates statistically distinct strata current SE approximation. Treat dashboard screening layer; follow dedicated helpers (plot_unexpected(), plot_displacement(), plot_interrater_agreement(), plot_facets_chisq()) detailed diagnosis.

Clusters points upper corners indicate systematic misfit patterns worth investigating. "severity" Ranked bar chart composite severity index top_n unexpected responses. title: Simulate long-format ordered many-facet data for design studies — simulate_mfrm_data
text: function generates synthetic ordered many-facet data RSM, PCM, package's bounded GPCM branch. data-generating process : Draw person abilities: \(\theta_n \sim N(0, \texttt{theta\_sd}^2)\) Draw rater severities: \(\delta_j \sim N(0, \texttt{rater\_sd}^2)\) Draw criterion difficulties: \(\beta_i \sim N(0, \texttt{criterion\_sd}^2)\) Generate evenly-spaced step thresholds spanning \(\pm\)step_span/2 observation, compute linear predictor \(\eta = \theta_n - \delta_j - \beta_i + \epsilon\) \(\epsilon \sim N(0, \texttt{noise\_sd}^2)\) (optional) Compute category probabilities recorded measurement model (RSM, PCM, bounded GPCM) sample response Latent-value generation explicit: latent_distribution = "normal" draws centered normal person/rater/ criterion values using supplied standard deviations latent_distribution = "empirical" resamples centered support values recorded sim_spec$empirical_support sim_spec$population$active = TRUE, person measures generated stored latent-regression population model template person covariates rather theta_sd dif_effects supplied, specified logit shift added \(\eta\) focal group target facet level, creating known DIF signal.  Similarly, interaction_effects injects known bias specific facet-level combinations. generator targets common two-facet rating design (persons \(\times\) raters \(\times\) criteria).  raters_per_person controls incomplete-block structure: less n_rater, person assigned rotating subset raters keep coverage balanced reproducible. Threshold handling intentionally explicit: thresholds = NULL, common equally spaced thresholds generated step_span thresholds numeric vector, used one common threshold set thresholds named list, numeric matrix, data frame, threshold values may vary StepFacet (currently Criterion Rater) bounded GPCM, generator requires explicit slope contract parallel threshold table. supported route keeps slope_facet == step_facet, normalizes supplied slopes geometric-mean-one log-slope identification used fit_mfrm(), samples responses corresponding GPCM category probabilities. Independent arbitrary slope-facet planning supported design, population-forecasting, diagnostic-screening, signal-detection helpers. Assignment handling also explicit: "crossed" uses full person x rater x criterion design "rotating" assigns deterministic rotating subset raters per person "sparse_linked" assigns persons incomplete rater subset assigns configurable set linking persons larger rater set "resampled" reuses empirical person-level rater profiles stored sim_spec$assignment_profiles, optionally carrying person-level Group "skeleton" reuses observed person--rater--criterion response skeleton stored sim_spec$design_skeleton, optionally carrying Group Weight Sparse linked simulation intended planned-missing rating designs connectivity maintained common linking persons. returned mfrm_sparse_design attribute summarizes design density, planned missingness, rater coverage, rater-pair common-person counts. summaries design diagnostics, model-fit statistics universal adequacy thresholds. branch follows sparse rater-mediated assessment design work Wind, Jones, Grajeda (2023, doi:10.1177/01466216231182148), Wind Jones (2018, doi:10.1177/0013164417703733), DeMars, Shapovalov, Hathcoat (2023). controlled workflows, build reusable simulation specification first via build_mfrm_sim_spec() derive one observed fit extract_mfrm_sim_spec(), pass sim_spec. Returned data include attributes: mfrm_truth: simulated true parameters (parameter-recovery checks) mfrm_truth$signals: injected DIF interaction signal tables mfrm_truth$slope_table: simulated discrimination table bounded GPCM mfrm_population_data: generated one-row-per-person background data simulation specification stores active latent-regression generator, including model-matrix xlevel contrast provenance categorical covariates mfrm_simulation_spec: generation settings (reproducibility) mfrm_sparse_design: sparse-design diagnostics assignment = "sparse_linked", including design density, planned missing rate, rater coverage, rater-pair common-person counts

code: toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core") keep_people <- unique(toy$Person)[1:18] toy_fit <- fit_mfrm(   toy[toy$Person %in% keep_people, , drop = FALSE],   "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",   method = "MML",   quad_points = 5,   maxit = 30 ) new_units <- data.frame(   Person = c("NEW01", "NEW01"),   Rater = unique(toy$Rater)[1],   Criterion = unique(toy$Criterion)[1:2],   Score = c(2, 3) ) pv <- sample_mfrm_plausible_values(toy_fit, new_units, n_draws = 3, seed = 1) summary(pv) #> mfrmr Plausible Values Summary #>   Calibration estimated by MML; scoring uses posterior EAP. Prior: Standard #>   normal N(0,1). #>   95% intervals: continuous posterior quantiles. #>   Posterior SDs and intervals condition on point estimates of the calibration #>   and prior; their estimation uncertainty is excluded. #>  #> Empirical draw summaries (first 10) #>  Person Draws MeanValue SDValue LowerValue UpperValue #>   NEW01     3    -0.373   0.323      -0.56          0 #>   Draw limits are empirical quantiles at the requested level. With few draws #>   they are coarse; use the companion posterior interval and its stated #>   calculation method for interval reporting. #>  #> Posterior estimates (first 10) #>  Person Estimate    SD  Lower Upper Observations                         Review #>   NEW01   -0.112 0.683 -1.448 1.235            2 No source restriction recorded #>  #> Response rows #>  InputRows KeptRows DroppedRows DroppedMissing DroppedBadScore DroppedBadWeight #>          2        2           0              0               0                0 #>  DroppedNonpositiveWeight #>                         0 #>   These draws are sampled from the quadrature-grid posterior under the existing #>   MML calibration and its fixed or adaptive integration setting. #>   Use them as approximate plausible-value summaries for posterior uncertainty, #>   not as deterministic future truth values. #>   Draws alone do not validate downstream group comparisons or regressions; #>   check the conditioning model and sampling design for the intended analysis. #>   Non-person facets in `new_data` must already exist in the fitted calibration. #>   Overlapping person IDs are treated as labels in `new_data`; the original #>   fitted person estimates are not updated. #>   The `draws` component contains quadrature-grid posterior draws that can be #>   used as approximate plausible-value summaries.

text: Linking, reporting, workflow visual-diagnostic tutorial figures now descriptive alternative text, including response-time views. Source archives include executed output figures fifteen tutorials. Extended-model help examples now reuse packaged synthetic fits, scores, diagnostics bootstrap results. Summaries, figures interval-level changes run immediately; expensive recomputation calls remain visible comments, complete regeneration script. Data, quadrature settings numerical checks preserved. 19 bootstrap trials illustrate workflow, accurate tail quantiles coverage guarantee. JML help examples previously stopped 30 iterations now allow sufficient iterations example data converge. estimator, data model specification unchanged; convergence warnings suppressed. ConQuest export help now explains local command-file workflow separate controls used posterior EAP calculations. Bundle guidance longer treats every inference-readiness restriction optimizer failure; numerical comparison remains distinct validation standard errors. workflow guide now distinguishes defaults change statistical analysis calculation display controls. opening example declares rubric bounds, preserved categories fixed ability population. Help clarifies testlet membership automatically add fixed difficulty effects, explicit dashboard misfit_warn replaces review bounds. Existing defaults unchanged. workflow guide README now explain function names show choose analysis concrete question. Extended-model scoring guidance points score_mfrm_persons() people already fitted model distinguishes model-specific meanings predict(). Help introductions clarify functions review supplied imputations, evaluate simulations, summarize attributes plan G/D studies. API names, arguments numerical methods unchanged. beginner output guide uses plainer questions longer describes particular plot mandatory.

title: mfrmr 0.2.4
text: Plot conversion now refuses unsupported PCA, clustering, pooled-MI, fixed-facet interval, screening-performance D-study difference views even component specified. Previously, option silently replace intended axes intervals generic bar chart. Multivariate D-study scenario conversion retains dedicated panels component = "series"; use plot_data() tables custom graphics. Non-supported views give guidance even ggplot2 installed. PCA score plots distinguish groups colour point shape retain encoding plot_data(). Scree plots distinguish retained omitted components filled open points, including monochrome output. Tutorial figures now include alternative text describing plotted target meaning intervals, missing results descriptive groups. mfrmr_output_guide() now includes "features", "imputation" "gtheory" routes, distinguishing dedicated tables, plots RDS saving fitted-model mfrm_results() reporting workflow. Extended-model interval plots testlet Person scoring now also work R sessions stats package installed attached. Help fit_mfrm_imputed() pool_mfrm_imputed() now renders function links code formatting correctly. Design-evaluation summaries retain full-precision metrics; digits now controls printing . Rounding can longer turn value just minimum, maximum, passing design recommendation.
